title: A Lexling in a basket
text: A basket turned up at the Lodge with a tag that said MILO and nothing else. He picked me in about four seconds. Maren says that never happens, and that she's never seen a Lexling like him.

title: A long first night
text: Milo ate half the sunberries, then looked up at the stars and said something slow and soft, like it mattered. I didn't understand a word. He fell asleep on my foot.

title: Into Whisperwood
text: Maren says Whisperwood is safe for beginners. Milo seems to think everything is safe, which is not the same thing.

title: The hungry Pebblit
text: A Pebblit was stuck under a berry bush it couldn't climb. We shared our sunberries. Before it left, it looked at Milo for a long time.

title: The Emberhog
text: An Emberhog came at us by the stream. Milo put its fire out. Afterwards it looked at Milo and said something slow and careful, like it meant every word. Then it ran.

title: Whispers
text: Two Puffkins in the trees went quiet when they saw Milo, then whispered to each other. Milo stayed close to me for the rest of the walk.

title: One element. One.
text: Maren went very quiet when I told her what Milo can do. "Lexlings have one element," she said. "One." She wants us to keep our ears open in Whisperwood. Lexlings have been restless all season, and she thinks they're talking to each other.

title: Milo's game
text: Milo lined up pinecones on a log and knocked them down one by one, announcing every shot like a show-off. When the last one rolled back at him, he threw up a wall of dirt and looked very pleased with himself.

title: A friendly spar
text: Pip wouldn't show us the way into the Old Hollow until Milo had sparred with Bluster. Bluster puffs himself up to twice his size before his biggest gust. Pip says Bluster was holding back.

title: The Old Hollow
text: Milo stopped me a step before the ground gave way. He moves through the Hollow like he's been somewhere like it before. I'm sure of it.

title: A light in the dark
text: A tiny Flickerwing was too scared to glow. Food didn't help. Milo just lay down next to it until it was brave enough. Now it rides in his fluff, lighting the way.

title: Words in stone
text: There are words carved into the standing stones in the Hollow. Real words, in the Lexlings' sounds. And under a carving of a small round creature with four marks on its brow, a name: MILO.

title: What the Craglings said
text: Two Craglings were talking behind the rocks. I caught bits: “piccolo”, “acqua”, “terra”, “aspettiamo”. I'm almost sure they were planning how to fight Milo.

title: Old Cinderback
text: The oldest Emberhog I've ever seen. It wanted Milo, and it called him “il piccolo”. When it lost, it said something to him, slow and almost sorry, and walked away into the dark.

title: The light, again
text: Milo said the thing about the light again. This time I understood more of it than I expected. Then he pressed against me and said something I understood completely.

title: Somebody wrote his name
text: Maren laid the rubbing next to the tag from Milo's basket. Same four letters. Same careful hand. Lexlings don't write, everyone knows that. Maren isn't so sure any more.

title: Camp
text: A tent, a fire ring and a very good log for sitting. Home.

title: Translators' Lodge
text: Creaky floors, a hundred notebooks and Lexlings in the rafters. Maren runs it.

title: Whisperwood
text: Tall trees, a cold stream and lots of small sounds you can't place. Milo can place all of them.

title: The Old Hollow
text: Standing stones, glowing mushrooms, and words carved where no human ever carved them.

title: First word
text: The first thing Milo ever said to me is the first thing he says to everyone.

title: Milo tells it his way
text: Back at camp Milo acted out the whole Emberhog fight. In his version he was much taller.

title: Another stone
text: Deeper in the Hollow, another carved stone. Above a carving of a small creature curled up asleep, someone cut words I could nearly follow. Milo didn't want to stay.
